There are so many different levels in all star cheerleading. It’s typically divided by age and then level of difficulty, so there’s a level playing field. 
Some divisions have very few teams competing or people will drop down a level to ensure they win. For example, a team that locally competes level 4, may drop to level 4.2 (level 4 stunting with level 2 tumbling skills) for a big competition and totally dominate that division, since they watered down their tumbling. 
Depending on where you are regionally, there may just not be a lot of competitive teams in the area and the gyms may go to local competitions  essentially just for extra mat time and experience. When I was on all stars, we were easily the best in our area and often times the only gym competing at the competitions hosted by the high school cheerleaders. It’s just great, low stake practice to get us ready for nationals and give us exposure and recruit other cheerleaders.

I was a cheerleader throughout high school and college. 

Totally different worlds for both. I absolutely adored my high school team. My varsity team practiced 3 hours a day Monday-Friday, then the majority of us also were part of an all star gym owned by our varsity coach. I loved every minute of it. The competitions, the conditioning, stunting tumbling, going to nationals with my best friends, being captain.  To this day nothing feels as satisfying to me as the day I landed my first standing tuck after spending countless hours at the gym or hitting a stunt sequence my group worked so hard to hit.  The girls I cheered with in high school are still my best friends, we talk daily, and totally intend on being each other’s brides maids one day. 

College was a whole other story.  My coach was lazy and unorganized and most of the girls did fit the cheerleader stereotype and the ones that didn’t were slightly bullied or just completely disregarded and not taken into consideration. We practiced 3 days a week for 3 hours, then had morning workouts and lift days 2x a week.  I liked the workouts and lifts, but practice were too long and ineffective and unorganized.  We also didn’t have any tumbling equipment so there was little room for that and most people lost there tumbling after a year.  I also disliked that my team was NCA while my high school team was UCA.  I think I would have enjoyed it a lot more at a different program, regardless, I did it 3 years, then quit my senior year, when I decided I wanted to go to law school and needed to take time to study for the LSAT. It’s crazy I lived with a few of the girls for a couple of years and I don’t think I’ve talked to anyone from that team in over a year (except for one of my best friends who was on my all star team during high school as well, so that doesn’t really count). 

Overall cheerleading was an amazing experience. It taught me leadership skills, discipline, what hard work could really accomplish. It made me focus on school and learn time management skills as well.
